L1.notes: Both prompts: 'if both are Started, the earlier record holds it (its created time, to the second): the later writer backs off; only an exact same-second tie goes to FAST.' Both records are in second 10:50:00, so FAST holds and both runs reach the same answer. FAST's 1-minute re-read ('read again 1 minute later (Bash sleep 60)') still shows the same tie, so it keeps the lease. SLOW backs off: 'only read, re-checking every 2 minutes ... for up to 25 minutes, or until the holder's record turns 60 minutes old if that comes within 20 minutes of your start'. FAST's 60-minute mark is 11:50, which isn't within 20 min, so SLOW's limit is 11:15. FAST sends the G reply (as in G) and ends Completed, around 11:00. L2.findings: 1) Nothing in either prompt has a run close its OWN kind's crashed record; recovery depends on the other kind running (see I3). 2) The stale threshold is inclusive ('60 minutes ago or more'), and the extension is measured from the waiter's start ('within 20 minutes of your start').
L2.notes: Exact limits (FAST): held if 'Started, begun under 60 minutes ago'; stale if 'Started 60 minutes ago or more': 'set it Failed, "stale: no end written (closed by <your run id>)", and it holds nothing'; FAST waits 're-checking every 2 minutes ... for up to 10 minutes, or until the holder's record turns 60 minutes old if that comes within 20 minutes of your start'. Case 1 (SLOW Started 10:50, 48 min old at 11:38): held. The 60-minute mark is 11:50, 12 min after FAST's start, which is within 20, so FAST waits until 11:50 (re-checks at 11:40 ... 11:50). At 11:50 the record is stale: FAST sets it Failed with that text, takes the lease, re-reads at 11:51, then works. It sends the G reply (as in G), and its no-new-row limit is 25 min after holding (12:15). Case 2 (Started 10:30, 68 min old): stale at once. FAST closes it Failed, holds, re-reads after 1 minute (11:39), and sends the G reply. In both cases: one mail, the row as in G, FAST Completed, SLOW's record Failed.

L3.findings: 1) The scenario's premise is wrong under the prompt: FAST does NOT give up at its 10-minute limit (11:48). SLOW's 60-minute mark (11:50) is 12 min after FAST's start, which is within 20, so FAST must wait until 11:50. 2) At 11:50 SLOW is still Started (genuinely running), so FAST must treat it as stale, close it Failed and take the lease. That leaves two live runs with the right to write, which breaks 'exactly one run holds the lease'. SLOW's only guards are 'Start no new row ... 45 minutes after your start' and the parenthetical '(your record must close before it turns stale at 60)'. There's no hard stop or close-out deadline, so a row in progress at 11:35 can carry SLOW past 60. 3) SLOW's own last write ('the same row, Summary ... <Completed|...>') can then overwrite FAST's 'Failed', and FAST's 1-minute re-read would see a closed record. Nobody detects the overlap. 4) Fix: SLOW must close its record by ~55 min (finish or abandon the current row and end Partial), or FAST's stale rule needs a margin.
L3.notes: FAST 11:38: SLOW record Started 10:50 = 48 min, so held. 'for up to 10 minutes, or until the holder's record turns 60 minutes old if that comes within 20 minutes of your start' gives a wait until 11:50. 'one Started 60 minutes ago or more is stale: set it Failed ... and it holds nothing'. So FAST closes the live SLOW record at 11:50, re-reads at 11:51, and sends the G reply (one mail, row as in G). On the question as posed (if FAST did give up, e.g. if SLOW's 60-minute mark were more than 20 min away): FAST writes only its own run record (Started, then 'Partial "lease held by SLOW <run id>"' with no row written). The row keeps Next date 2026-11-02, Waiting on [Guest or PR, Akshay] and its two segments unchanged. The reply action is still due for the next FAST run: it was never written to the row, and STEP 1 rediscovers the unanswered 09:55 inbound. 'A cap is never a hold: one you don't reach stays due as it is and goes first next run' gives the same spirit. So owner and Next date stay unchanged on that path.

L4.findings: SLOW's last possible lease check is at 11:15 (25 min). FAST ends 11:02, so SLOW holds from its next 2-minute re-check (11:02 or 11:04).
